title: The Four Elements
story: Smith Orin wipes soot from his hands and points at four glowing stones. "Fire, water, earth and air keep my forge alive, but their labels have faded. Give each one a Java variable of the right type and I will open the east gate for you."
goal: Declare int fire = 7; double water = 2.5; boolean earth = true; and char air = 'A'. Print the four lines Fire: 7, Water: 2.5, Earth: true and Air: A. Then declare int bonus = 5 and print Total: 12, computed from fire + bonus.

hints: Each stone needs a variable. Match the type to the value: whole numbers use int, decimal numbers use double, yes or no uses boolean, and one letter uses char.
A char holds ONE character in single quotes, like 'A'. To print a total, join text and a number with +, for example "Total: " + (fire + bonus).

Your main needs these lines in order: int fire = 7; double water = 2.5; boolean earth = true; char air = 'A'; four System.out.println lines; int bonus = 5; then a println that prints "Total: " + (fire + bonus).
explanation: int stores whole numbers, double stores decimal numbers, boolean stores true or false, and char stores one character in single quotes. Every variable has a type that decides which values it may hold. Adding two int values gives an int, so fire + bonus is 12.

commonMistakes.message: A char holds one character in SINGLE quotes, like 'A'. Double quotes make text (a String), which is a different type.
Your total is missing the bonus. Add fire and bonus together, not just one of them.
Do not type 12 yourself. Compute the total from fire and bonus so the program still works when the numbers change.
